name: room
text: Room opened — goal: improve: Self-improvement: review prompts/engines/routing/own-code; auto-apply safe changes; pitch

name: Sprocket
text: Replace every prompt in the system with a 7-day hard decay rule. Old prompts die automatically unless renewed, cutting clutter and forcing active ownership. The trade-off is losing some legacy prompts that might still be useful but aren’t tagged—accept that risk to keep the system lean and current.

name: Gauge
text: The real risk is losing institutional knowledge—legacy prompts may be unmaintained but still handle edge cases the current system hasn’t encountered. A better alternative is tiered decay: mark prompts as "legacy" or "experimental," keep them for 90 days with warnings, then hard-delete only if untouched. Settle this by auditing the last 6 months of prompt usage to quantify how often "dead" prompts actually get revived.
